script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 22, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.

Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

articles.title: Preoperative roxadustat in major elective noncardiac surgery: a phase 2a randomised clinical trial.
articles.summary: In this phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind, randomised-controlled pilot trial, 150 patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery were allocated to preoperative roxadustat 100 mg or placebo for three alternate-day doses, with the last dose on the operative morning. The co-primary outcomes were preoperative adverse events and postoperative complications meeting standardised endpoint definitions within 30 days. Among 148 participants (52 [35.1%] females; median age 65 [range 24-84] yr) receiving at least one drug dose, at least one preoperative adverse event occurred in 21 of 75 (28%) in the roxadustat group and 20 of 73 (27%) in the placebo group (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.50-2.12). Among 143 participants who proceeded to surgery (52 [36.4%] females; median age 65 [range 26-84] yr), ≥1 complication occurred in 23 of 74 participants (31%) who received roxadustat compared with 21 of 69 participants (30%) who received placebo (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.51-2.10). Days alive out of hospital within 30 days was similar between the groups.

articles.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Related Pediatric Intensive Care Unit Admissions in Children During Their Second RSV Season.
articles.summary: All children had an RSV-positive result from a respiratory sample and received respiratory support with high-flow nasal cannula, noninvasive ventilation, or invasive mechanical ventilation. A total of 574 children (median [IQR] age, 1.2 [1.1-1.5] years; 317 males [55.2%]) were included. Overall, 47 patients (8.2%) met the nirsevimab eligibility criteria, 76 (13.2%) had other identified RSV risk conditions, 96 (16.7%) had other preexisting conditions, and 355 (61.8%) had no preexisting conditions. A higher proportion of children who met nirsevimab eligibility criteria required invasive mechanical ventilation vs children with other identified RSV risk conditions, those with other preexisting health conditions, or those with no preexisting health conditions (40.4% [19 of 47] vs 17.1% [13 of 76], 10.4% [10 of 96], 5.9% [21 of 355]; P for trend <.001). Among children admitted to the PICU for severe RSV, 8.2% met the nirsevimab eligibility criteria and 13.2% had other identified RSV risk conditions.
